note: Triennial election of the Dungannon rural district councillors, 1933. 'There will be no contest in any of the district electoral divisions of Dungannon Rural Council' (Ulster Herald, 22 April 1933, p. 5); the nominations list is printed in the Irish News, 19 April 1933, p. 6 (one name for each division; read on the page image, council-audit, Nov 2026). Eleven of the nineteen divisions are recorded by the meeting method (7 Nov 2026): each member is the 1930 return for the division and sat at the new council's statutory meeting on Tuesday 6 June 1933 (Mid-Ulster Mail, 10 June 1933, p. 5). Not recorded: Altmore, Clonavaddy, Crossdernott, Donaghmore and Granville (the 1930 members are not named at the meeting); Minterburn (Mr. M. Busby, the member from 1936, sits, not the 1930 member); Castlecaulfield (Colonel Howard and Mr. M. D. Brown both sit, and a Mr. M. Brown was co-opted); and Anahoe (both Mr. T. D. Givans and Mr. T. J. Cuddy appear). No poll was held; Tyrone's polling day was Wednesday 31 May 1933. The Irish News nominations list prints "Killyman, Mr. Robert Carroll" (and Mr. J. R. Erskine, J.P., the 1930 member, for Granville); Carroll was the only nominee and was returned unopposed. He held Killyman again in 1936. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Corrected from the page image of Irish News, 19 April 1933, p. 6 (council-audit, Nov 2026): the member was J. R. Erskine, inferred from the 1930 return; the nominations list names Robert Carroll for Killyman and puts Erskine in Granville.
